question: Do public official sources support separate Sakang River and Tagkawayan River research leads, and did a bounded public search retrieve river-specific fish evidence?
purpose: Extend the CALABARZON freshwater denominator from source-backed river names while keeping water-district route descriptions, fish presence, current water use, and geometry separate.
searchMethod: On 2026-11-01, searched public indexes for Sakang River/Tagkawayan fish, freshwater fish surveys in Tagkawayan, and CvSU-library thesis records. Checked official Tagkawayan Water District history text and the official LGU local-news index. The Water District page returned a search-index excerpt but a direct open check failed with a cache-miss error; the LGU index returned HTTP 403. This bounded search is not evidence of fish absence or of no unpublished study.

findings.sakangIdentity: The undated Tagkawayan Water District history page names Sakang River as a surface-water source, describes its origin as approximately 3 km north of Poblacion, and says it flows southeast, joining creeks and emptying into Tagkawayan River. The page also reports a 25 L/s discharge without a measurement date. Treat these as undated source descriptions, not current utility status, a verified route, or a current flow value.
findings.tagkawayanRiverIdentity: The same Water District description separately names Tagkawayan River as the receiving watercourse. Sakang River and Tagkawayan River are therefore retained as separate source-named leads; no mapped connection or full channel extent is inferred.
findings.recentLocalityContext: The official Tagkawayan LGU local-news index reports a 25 March 2026 tree-planting activity on Sakang River in Barangay San Vicente. This supports recent use of the feature name and barangay context, not fish sampling, river geometry, or water quality.
findings.fishEvidenceSearch: The bounded public search did not retrieve a Sakang- or Tagkawayan-River-specific finfish survey or checklist. Results included unrelated municipal marine-fishery material and a national freshwater checklist, neither of which is assigned to these rivers. This does not establish fish absence or checklist completeness.
findings.waterAndSafetyLimits: No dated fish observation, field-identification method, voucher, station crosswalk, salinity reading, current abstraction status, water-quality/safety result, legal fishing rule, or verified geometry was retrieved.

accessAndRights.waterDistrict: Official Tagkawayan Water District history page; page date/refresh and item-specific reuse terms were not established. Direct open check returned a cache-miss error; only the indexed source text was reviewed.
accessAndRights.lgu: Official Municipality of Tagkawayan local-news index; the 25 March 2026 excerpt was reviewed, while direct page access returned HTTP 403. No item-specific reuse terms were identified.
accessAndRights.rawRetention: No page copies, map images, coordinates, route data, or survey tables were retained.

nextAction: Seek dated, station-resolved, rights-cleared freshwater fish evidence for both river leads and an official route/map source for each channel. Do not convert the Water District narrative into GIS geometry or the reported 25 L/s into a current measurement.

sources.supports: Water District indexed history text for Sakang River name, approximate source location/flow narrative, receiving Tagkawayan River name, and undated reported discharge.
Official LGU indexed local-news item dated 25 March 2026 naming Sakang River in Barangay San Vicente during a tree-planting activity.
